title: Prove sharp seven- and nine-line rational anchor-box floors
body:
Nine rational lines with three totals, nonzero diagonal pairings and nonempty canonical tied sets admit an anchor box of **six**. The same proof gives **five** at seven lines. Exact duplications of Aaron Wang's PR #2978 core attain both bounds.

The new analytic matrix theorem works over **any field**: a rank-at-most-three nine-by-nine matrix with nonzero diagonal has disjoint ordered nonzero blocks of sizes **3+3 or 4+2**. A six-row dichotomy, seven-row consequence and exchange across two diagonal bases prove the result. PR #3409's asymmetric label construction transfers it to the rational box contract. The alternative 4+2 matters: `diag(J5,J2,J2)` refutes the narrower claim that two disjoint triples must always exist.

The focused package is `research/fstar-nine-line-floor/`, containing the proof, exact constructor, sharp fixtures, finite controls, source pins and open next questions. The sharpness argument is analytic: a box meeting all three fixture blocks would require a rank-three binary label-dot matrix with target labels in a two-dimensional space.

Validation: registered Python 3.12.15 normal and isolated/optimized/warnings-as-errors replay, package metadata/source pins, exact frozen-source lineage, publication source history and whitespace checks. The controls exercise directed ordering, the rank/diagonal/tie/parity hypotheses, both cycle-minor branches, diagonal-basis reconstruction, bipartite-family classification, and counterfeit-source rejection before execution. Same-session agent audits checked the argument and package; these are not human acceptance or formal proof checks.

Attribution: DreamingOfClouds's PR #1590/#2111 definitions, Aaron Wang/navinor's PR #2914/#2978/#3031 box/SG/core lineage, the related Arham Tahir PR #3105 classification, and the PR #3332/#3393/#3409 finite-floor work are retained. The independent oracle is copied unchanged from corrected PR #3393 at `8e1e574fa68465dc0ec69d07852266b9597f9597`; it is reused checking code, not a newly independent implementation. Exact provenance is in `SOURCES.json`.

Coordination: [canonical claim and handoff](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-19009093). This continues PR #3409's nine-line question from refreshed canonical main; no selected-frontier change.

Limits: analytic proof, not formal verification or an exhaustive matrix census. Nonempty ties remain an explicit hypothesis. The full F-star supplier and the eleven-line floor-seven question remain open; κ is unchanged.
